Routes and operating conditions for a stable pDAI
30 September 2026. Study of the coordinated proposal. This is a synthesis of saved evidence and offline
design reasoning; no new blockchain calls or transactions were made for this edition.
Scope and definitions
This study enumerates every accounting route family identified in the recovered research. It is not an
inventory of every possible future deployment, an exhaustive pARB application catalogue or a claim that
every route currently operates. The destination Curve pool census covers 619 distinct pools returned by
eight responsive roots at PulseChain block 27,675,130, hash 
0xdd12f23ad571882b63fd333c5d3909a45a05fe6f0a3c2b273cb7e1e6b0917954. Other supporting studies retain their own
block identities. Historical observations are not synchronized into a fictional single live state.
“Observed” below means a saved destination getter, source condition or balance supports the narrow
statement. “Conditional” means the complete route depends on unresolved predicates. “Proposed”
means a design rather than a demonstrated deployment. Contract identities, rights and obligations
survive consolidation; claims between controlled entities are eliminated when calculating net resources.

F2/F3 include transferable vault shares or position claims, including NFT s where a compatible buyer,
lender or adapter makes them usable. F7/F14 may use flash credit for a local cycle repaying principal
and fees in the same transaction. Delayed bridge reimbursement cannot repay that same atomic loan
afterward. See the receipt and validator study (Appendix 49). These are variants, not new independent
budgets.
A source protocol name does not make a route viable. The next source inventory must record chain/RPC,
contract address, active implementation, deposit token, receipt token, redeemability, beneficiary rights,
oracle, limits, and supported bridge output. The issuer destination then needs an exact collateral
address and functioning acceptance path. Until that inventory exists, F1–F3 are architectural routes, not
a verified list of all L2 protocols.

A funded fixed-rate converter is conceptually distinct from V2 reserve-ratio pricing. Maker's historical 
PSM implementation supplies a documented example with collateral exchange and mint/burn
permissions. No copied PSM route, pDAI mint authority or new converter deployment is established here.
An inventory-only converter would need both owned pDAI and payment assets; its quotes cease when
either side is exhausted.
A simple proposed operating rule
This is a controller specification, not deployed code. An operator submits actions; contracts execute
submitted transactions. Preserve support and settlement commitments before optional yield. The
reference must be defined before any “below” or “above” comparison. A local reference requires
executable parity; a dollar reference also requires independent economic validation. For dollar parity,
payment units per pDAI equal one dollar divided by the reliably measured dollar price of the payment
asset, before costs. Revalue coverage when that price changes. Fixed local parity is a separate promise.
Time-weighted observations measure a market history and cannot make a frozen accounting number
payable. The Uniswap oracle documentation describes cumulative observation mechanics, not a dollar
guarantee.

executable quotes

pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 402

The proposed ten-second cadence is an allocation schedule, not a promise of inclusion in every block or
a guarantee that an old quote remains executable. Each eligible action must respect current funds, size
limits, fees and settlement commitments. Record skipped slots explicitly rather than treating unspent
allocations as completed purchases. Transaction ordering and competition can worsen realized execution
even when a prior quote was favorable.
Below target, buy with the least costly usable route within the allocated budget. Above target, sell
owned transferable pDAI; issuer minting of OUSD or eUSD does not itself mint pDAI. Inside the band,
avoid spending simply because a slot arrived. Use net surplus to relieve shared-pool shortages, earn
collectible income or reduce liabilities according to priorities defined in advance.
Measure capacity without counting resources twice
Define a horizon H, a payment asset, a permitted execution band and the maximum cumulative outside
selling and buying flow to be supported. The commitment must address repeated trades, not just one
marginal quote. Define permitted outages and the response time during them.
Report:
Execution: net payment proceeds or purchase cost for a fixed ladder of sizes, including an
illustrative 50m-pDAI case where relevant.
Price: reference deviation, observation window and target-restoration time.
Immediate liquidity: owned immediately deliverable payment units and pDAI; encumbered and
delayed resources listed separately.
Solvency: realizable consolidated assets versus enforceable outside liabilities; show stressed
recoveries separately. System-owned pDAI at its defended price is not independent counterasset
backing.
Obligations: borrower debt, Portal unbacked principal, issuer collateral promises, bridge
reimbursement and existing LP/credit commitments in their own denominations.
Income: collectible outside proceeds less all costs and losses; internal transfers eliminated.
Exposure: outside float plus credible future mints, unlocks, borrowing and bridge arrivals over H.
Do not add an LP share's value to its underlying assets, a wrapped receipt to the same aT oken, or a
Reserve/Origin/mStable output to its collateral as independent capital. Buying pDAI changes portfolio
composition; it does not automatically create profit. Paying an external user removes payment capacity.
New buyer inflows replenish it only when actually received.
The arithmetic deliverable payment units / promised payment units over H is a useful fixed-rate coverage
indicator under matching units and explicit netting assumptions. It does not establish a V2 slippage
bound. V2 needs reserves, fee and ordering calculations; a yield forecast does not count as immediately
deliverable reserves. Saved stability (Appendix 60) and liquidity (Appendix 40) models retain their toy
assumptions and are not reclassified as live capacity.

The claims and authority map (Appendix 29) is the detailed register. This table does not certify which
person controls an address. No changes were attempted, no keys accessed and no state-changing
simulations executed.
Reproduce without altering frozen results
The offline issuer analyzer rewrites catalogues in its --folder directory. Copy the saved issuer evidence to
a fresh explicit artifact batch before rerunning it; never point a reproduction run at the frozen original.
Retain corrected inputs, excluded malformed batches and their recorded hashes. The issuer study
(Appendix 38) gives the decoder command and input identity. Published getter/source statements and
proposed controller rules remain distinct.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 404

Stress cases and completeness boundary
Evaluate sustained selling, sustained buying, shared-counterasset depeg, stale valuation, failed
collateral redemption, bridge outage, missing operator responses, fees exceeding income, source
issuance increases and scarce base-pool inventory. A frozen price feed is a failure of economic
measurement even when the contract accepts it. A pause can preserve remaining resources while
making conversion unavailable; availability must be part of the promised service.
The specific stress magnitudes, target band, H, funded balances and loss policy are not yet chosen. No
new live-capacity test was performed for this synthesis. A complete economic validation would need
those quantities, all applicable authority and bridge predicates, and independent review of the deployed
implementations. Agreement between reviews can improve this document and find contradictions. It
cannot validate an unknown deployment, turn a conditional forecast into measured income, or prove
flawlessness.
Compare out-of-band execution, unavailable conversion time and settlement shortfalls at the same
budget, sizes and horizon. No optimal result or statistical confidence has been measured.
The simplest candidate is a named reference, one or a few functioning funding routes, both inventories,
sufficient accessible depth and an explicit response rule. Additional mechanisms should earn their place
by adding measured capacity or independent resilience.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 405

A simple proposed operating rule
This is a controller specification, not deployed code. An operator submits actions; contracts execute
submitted transactions. Preserve support and settlement commitments before optional yield. The
reference must be defined before any “below” or “above” comparison. A local reference requires
executable parity; a dollar reference also requires independent economic validation. For dollar parity,
payment units per pDAI equal one dollar divided by the reliably measured dollar price of the payment
asset, before costs. Revalue coverage when that price changes. Fixed local parity is a separate promise.
Time-weighted observations measure a market history and cannot make a frozen accounting number
payable. The Uniswap oracle documentation describes cumulative observation mechanics, not a dollar
guarantee.

The proposed ten-second cadence is an allocation schedule, not a promise of inclusion in every block or
a guarantee that an old quote remains executable. Each eligible action must respect current funds, size
limits, fees and settlement commitments. Record skipped slots explicitly rather than treating unspent
allocations as completed purchases. Transaction ordering and competition can worsen realized execution
even when a prior quote was favorable.
Below target, buy with the least costly usable route within the allocated budget. Above target, sell
owned transferable pDAI; issuer minting of OUSD or eUSD does not itself mint pDAI. Inside the band,
avoid spending simply because a slot arrived. Use net surplus to relieve shared-pool shortages, earn
collectible income or reduce liabilities according to priorities defined in advance.
Measure capacity without counting resources twice
Define a horizon H, a payment asset, a permitted execution band and the maximum cumulative outside
selling and buying flow to be supported. The commitment must address repeated trades, not just one
marginal quote. Define permitted outages and the response time during them.
Report:
Execution: net payment proceeds or purchase cost for a fixed ladder of sizes, including an
illustrative 50m-pDAI case where relevant.
Price: reference deviation, observation window and target-restoration time.
Immediate liquidity: owned immediately deliverable payment units and pDAI; encumbered and
delayed resources listed separately.
Solvency: realizable consolidated assets versus enforceable outside liabilities; show stressed
recoveries separately. System-owned pDAI at its defended price is not independent counterasset
backing.
Obligations: borrower debt, Portal unbacked principal, issuer collateral promises, bridge
reimbursement and existing LP/credit commitments in their own denominations.
Income: collectible outside proceeds less all costs and losses; internal transfers eliminated.
Exposure: outside float plus credible future mints, unlocks, borrowing and bridge arrivals over H.
Do not add an LP share's value to its underlying assets, a wrapped receipt to the same aT oken, or a
Reserve/Origin/mStable output to its collateral as independent capital. Buying pDAI changes portfolio
composition; it does not automatically create profit. Paying an external user removes payment capacity.
New buyer inflows replenish it only when actually received.
The arithmetic deliverable payment units / promised payment units over H is a useful fixed-rate coverage
indicator under matching units and explicit netting assumptions. It does not establish a V2 slippage
bound. V2 needs reserves, fee and ordering calculations; a yield forecast does not count as immediately
deliverable reserves. Saved stability (Appendix 60) and liquidity (Appendix 40) models retain their toy
assumptions and are not reclassified as live capacity.

Stress cases and completeness boundary
Evaluate sustained selling, sustained buying, shared-counterasset depeg, stale valuation, failed
collateral redemption, bridge outage, missing operator responses, fees exceeding income, source
issuance increases and scarce base-pool inventory. A frozen price feed is a failure of economic
measurement even when the contract accepts it. A pause can preserve remaining resources while
making conversion unavailable; availability must be part of the promised service.
The specific stress magnitudes, target band, H, funded balances and loss policy are not yet chosen. No
new live-capacity test was performed for this synthesis. A complete economic validation would need
those quantities, all applicable authority and bridge predicates, and independent review of the deployed
implementations. Agreement between reviews can improve this document and find contradictions. It
cannot validate an unknown deployment, turn a conditional forecast into measured income, or prove
flawlessness.
Compare out-of-band execution, unavailable conversion time and settlement shortfalls at the same
budget, sizes and horizon. No optimal result or statistical confidence has been measured.
The simplest candidate is a named reference, one or a few functioning funding routes, both inventories,
sufficient accessible depth and an explicit response rule. Additional mechanisms should earn their place
by adding measured capacity or independent resilience.
